speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To help me understand your condition, have you noticed any yellowing of your skin or eyes, or changes in the color of your urine or stool?

speaker: Patient
text: 32-year-old male. The patient reports a 2-month history of increasing generalized fatigue and severe pruritus. He has known hypertension and was diagnosed with ulcerative colitis 5 years ago. He mentions being sexually active with 2 female partners and inconsistent condom use.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you have a history of jaundice, pale stools, or dark urine, and have you noticed any weight loss or abdominal pain?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Generalized fatigue and severe pruritus. I also have Scleral icterus, Multiple scratch marks on trunk and extremities.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of ulcerative colitis and these symptoms, I suspect a complication affecting your bile ducts. REQUEST TEST: MRCP

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the normal MRCP, I am concerned about small duct disease rather than large duct obstruction. REQUEST TEST: Anti-mitochondrial antibodies

speaker: Doctor
text: Let me clarify your alcohol consumption habits and any recent travel history, as well as whether you have been taking any new medications or herbal supplements. Have you experienced any fever, night sweats, or unintentional weight loss?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Hypertension, Ulcerative Colitis Social history: Sexually active with inconsistent condom use

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the negative AMA and normal MRCP, I need to rule out autoimmune hepatitis or viral hepatitis. REQUEST TEST: Hepatitis B surface antigen, Hepatitis C antibody, and Anti-smooth muscle antibodies

speaker: Doctor
text: Since viral and large-duct causes are ruled out, I suspect primary sclerosing cholangitis affecting the small ducts, which is strongly associated with ulcerative colitis. REQUEST TEST: Liver biopsy

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Histology shows concentric periductal fibrosis ("onion-skinning") around the interlobular bile ducts, consistent with primary sclerosing cholangitis.
